nominees.name: Sheperd S. Doeleman

nominees.name: James M. Moran
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

subfield: Astrophysics / high-energy astrophysics and radio interferometry
motivation: The nominees conceived and built an instrument that many thought impossible: an Earth-sized millimetre-wavelength interferometer with the angular resolution to resolve the event horizon of a black hole. Falcke predicted in 2000 that the shadow of Sgr A* would be observable at submillimetre wavelengths. Moran pioneered the techniques of very-long-baseline interferometry on which the array rests. Doeleman led the technical development, the first horizon-scale detections (2008) and the founding of the collaboration. In 2019 the Event Horizon Telescope imaged the shadow of the black hole in M87, and in 2022 the shadow of Sgr A*. These images confirmed the general-relativistic prediction of a photon ring around a dark shadow whose size matches the mass, and polarimetric images have since revealed ordered magnetic fields that launch relativistic jets. This new observational window directly tests strong-field gravity and accretion physics, and it has transformed high-energy astrophysics.
